items.prompt: Monday morning. You ask a friend about the weekend that just ended:
options: ¿Qué vas a hacer el fin de semana?
items.explanation: ¿Qué tal el fin de semana? asks how a weekend went.
optionNotes: This asks what your friend usually does on weekends.
This asks about plans for the next weekend.
This is not a natural question.

items.prompt: You had a great time at a party. You say:
items.explanation: “Have a good time” is pasarlo bien (Latin America also: pasarla bien): Lo pasé muy bien.
optionNotes: A word-for-word translation of “I had a good time”; Spanish does not say this.
This means “The weather was very good”.
Me pasó means “it happened to me”; this is not Spanish.

items.prompt:
—Fui a Cuba de vacaciones y lo pasé genial.
—___
items.explanation: ¡Qué suerte! (Lucky you!) reacts to good news.
optionNotes: This asks about plans, not about the trip.

items.prompt: ___ fuimos al museo, después comimos y al final volvimos al hotel.
items.explanation: A story starts with primero, goes on with después or luego and ends with al final.
optionNotes: Al final is for the last action, and the sentence already has one.
